$comment: How a build of the ray tracer is configured, and how its tests run, in the form CMake and every IDE
read. `omw` is the one way in on the desk and in CI: it configures through these, fetches what a
system lacks first, and knows what each flavour is for once it is built. A visible preset is a
flavour on a system, named `<flavour>-<system>`, and inherits the flavour, the system and the common
ground, in that order: the earlier preset wins a variable both name. The hidden presets are the parts
and build nothing alone, and each flavour's names its directory, `build-<flavour>`, which is where
`omw` looks for it. Version 10, because it is the first that can carry a `$comment` beside each
decision.

configurePresets.name: rtx
$comment: Common to every flavour. The content tools upstream builds by default stay off where no flavour
reads them: the CS, the wizard and the two importers are Qt and ESM code this fork does not touch.
`omw setup` turns the ini importer on for the one build that writes an openmw.cfg. ccache drives
GCC and MSVC alike, and the compile database is what an editor reads.

configurePresets.name: linux
$comment: What Linux supplies: recastnavigation and Google Test as packages, and mold to link with.
`RelWithDebInfo` is `-O2 -g` here and not CMake's own, which carries `-DNDEBUG` and compiles
out every assert in the tree — the debug flavours are the one build anybody develops in.
**Static libraries are thin archives** (`ar T`), a list of the objects where they lie: the game's
is 1.3 GB of objects with their debug data, and copied whole it took six seconds of every build
that changed one of them, before any of the three programs on it could link. No library is
installed, so none has to carry its objects anywhere.

configurePresets.name: windows
$comment: What Windows supplies: upstream's prebuilt vcpkg set, which `omw` fetches into deps/ at the tag
CI/deps_versions.msvc.sh pins and names here through VCPKG_TAG. The set carries neither
recastnavigation, Google Test, SQLite nor yaml-cpp, so CMake fetches those, and no Qt, so the
launcher stays unbuilt. Its SDL2 is built without Vulkan and refuses the renderer's window at
runtime, so SDL's own package of the same version stands in, fetched beside the set and named
through RTX_SDL2_VERSION; vcpkg's copying of DLLs beside a binary is off, since it would put its
SDL2 back over SDL's on every link, and `omw` copies the runtime once. Upstream's precompiled
headers are off because ccache cannot see through them: with them on, 593 of 623 compiles of the
backend were 'could not use precompiled header' and the cache held nothing. `RelWithDebInfo` is
`-O2 -Z7`, MSVC's `-O2 -g`: MSVC's own carries `/DNDEBUG` exactly as GCC's carries `-DNDEBUG`,
and `-Z7` writes the debug data into the object, which is the one form ccache can cache.
Alone, without `omw` exporting the two versions, the paths below name nothing.

configurePresets.name: no-tools
$comment: The content tools and the launcher, off. A flavour that never runs them leaves them out: a
sanitizer build of Qt code this fork does not touch doubles the wait for nothing, and the
measured build builds what is measured. The debug flavour keeps them, so that the launcher's
own [RTX] page can be compiled on request.

configurePresets.name: debug
configurePresets.$comment: Every assert, with the tests: the everyday build.

configurePresets.name: release
$comment: `-O3 -DNDEBUG`, no tests: the build a number is quoted from. Nothing measured is measured
through a test. Each system adds the light debug data and the frame pointers a profiler
needs, in its own spelling, on the visible preset.

configurePresets.name: asan
$comment: The debug flavour under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, the two upstream runs
its tests under. Linux only: MSVC has a sanitizer, and nobody has measured this tree under it.
The ASAN_OPTIONS without which there is no device, and the UBSAN_OPTIONS that make a finding a
failure, are its test preset's.

configurePresets.name: plain
$comment: The tree without the ray tracer, as upstream builds it: every program, the CS and its tests
among them, the three test suites and the benchmarks. What proves that the tree still builds and
passes upstream's own suites where the fork's renderer is not built, with the stub renderer and
`OPENMW_RTX=0` in place of the ray tracer. `OPENMW_CXX_FLAGS` comes from the environment, where CI
puts upstream's `-Werror` and a desk with a newer compiler puts nothing. Listed first among what
a visible preset inherits, so what it turns on beats what `rtx` and `windows` turn off.

configurePresets.name: package
$comment: What a release archive holds: the release build with every assert out, the launcher, the wizard
and the two importers a player meets, and no tests. `OPENMW_LOCAL_INSTALL` is upstream's portable
layout, everything in one directory with relative paths, which is what the archive is; the
binaries find their openmw.cfg beside themselves wherever the directory is put. The CS stays off,
as the `rtx` preset says. Listed first among what a visible preset inherits, so what it turns
on beats what `windows` turns off.

configurePresets.name: debug-linux
configurePresets.$comment: The test binaries at `-Og`, which `cmake/Tests.cmake` says why of.

configurePresets.name: release-linux
$comment: `-g1` is line tables and nothing else, so it costs nothing at runtime and a profile can name a
line rather than an offset; the frame pointers cost less than the run-to-run spread and are
what let perf walk a stack for the price of reading it. Both on the measured build rather
than on a profiling build beside it, because two binaries means the profile explains a frame
the benchmark did not time.

configurePresets.name: release-windows
$comment: `-Z7` with `-DEBUG` at link is the line table a profiler names a line from, and `-Oy-` keeps the
frame pointers a stack walk reads. Spelt with a dash, which every Microsoft tool takes, because
Git Bash turns `/O2` into `C:/Program Files/Git/O2` on its way to cmake. Through
`CMAKE_<LANG>_FLAGS_INIT`, which CMake appends its platform's own to — `/EHsc` and `/machine:x64`
among them — where `CMAKE_<LANG>_FLAGS` set outright would drop them.

configurePresets.name: plain-windows
configurePresets.$comment: Qt for the CS, the launcher and the wizard, and the link-time optimisation upstream's Windows build takes.

configurePresets.name: package-linux
$comment: `-g1`, function names and line tables and nothing else, for the symbols `omw archive`
publishes beside the AppImage: a player's crash dump then names a function and a line. It costs
nothing at runtime.

configurePresets.name: package-windows
$comment: Qt, which the set has none of and the launcher and the wizard are made of: the one `omw` fetches
into deps/ for this flavour, by the version CI/deps_versions.msvc.sh pins and exports as QT_VER.
`-Z7` with `-DEBUG` at link writes each executable's PDB beside it in the build, for the symbols
`omw archive` publishes beside the folder; the install rules leave the PDBs behind.

testPresets.name: tests
$comment: What every run of the suites `cmake/Tests.cmake` registers shares: a failing test's output on the
page, and a build that registers none a failure rather than a pass. `omw test` picks the labels.

testPresets.name: sanitizers
$comment: **`protect_shadow_gap=0` is not a preference: without it there is no device at all.** The NVIDIA
driver maps its own enormous address ranges, ASan's shadow gap is mapped `PROT_NONE` across part of
what it wants, and `vkCreateDevice` comes back `VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED`, which every RTX
test would read as a skip. What it costs is the guard page that catches a wild pointer landing in
the gap. **The leak check is off, since the driver's allocations are not this fork's**: the
driver, the loader, the layers and dbus keep a heap for the life of the process, and each would be
reported with a stack the fork does not appear in. A finding is a failure, with the stack that led
to it, as upstream runs its tests. What the caller's own environment names comes last and wins:
`ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1` turns the leak check back on. `omw` runs every program of the asan
flavour under this, and not the tests alone.
